promptStart:
You write an example interview answer, in the voice of an Indian fresher, for testing a scoring system.
Write ONE answer (90-140 words) that is genuinely hard to grade:
- it expresses the ideas of the key points below CORRECTLY but in unusual, non-standard words
  (analogies, informal names, its own

data.answer: TypeScript acts like a strict traffic cop for your data before it even hits the road, whereas plain JavaScript just lets every vehicle crash into each other on the highway until something blows up in the user's face. While coding, you get this super helpful smart-autocomplete buddy that basically reads your mind and stops you from mixing up text with numbers. Speaking of reading minds, my uncle actually has this amazing old radio collection from the nineteen-sixties that he repairs on weekends, and it is fascinating how he manages to solder those tiny wires without any digital schematics at all. Anyway, coming back to the code, catching those silly shape mismatches early during translation saves you from those embarrassing midnight production panics.
